raw_response:
I have 0.12 hectares of sorghum intercropped on my farm here in Benshagul Gumuz. Because I had some schooling, I know fertilizer helps, but money is tight and this plot is small, so I will get just a little DAP from the cooperative—about enough for 30 kilograms of nitrogen per hectare. I will also spread manure from our animals on this plot, and I will sow the local sorghum seed I kept from last harvest since improved sorghum seed is hard to find and costly. We do not spray chemicals or irrigate because we depend on the rains, and my family can manage the weeding and harvesting ourselves without hiring anyone—around 12 days of work spread across the season.
